milestone: Allocation rules: need score, C3-C6 ranking, token mapping, diagnostics

registered.need_window_definition: K = number of leading iterations in which every token runs; labels assigned after iteration K - 1

tie_rules.C3: g descending, then token ID ascending
tie_rules.C4: (1 + lambda m) g descending (float64, exact), then token ID ascending
tie_rules.C5: m descending, then position in torch.randperm(N) seeded by the prompt ID
tie_rules.C6: b descending, then g descending, then token ID ascending

registered.small_resolution_groups: registered high-group share, rounded (31 of 192 tiny tokens, 312 of 1,950 real tokens)

device_scope: The need score and every model test run on CPU and MPS. Ranking (numpy lexsort in float64), token mapping and the diagnostics run on CPU by design, so their results do not depend on the device.
t12_note: The literal T12 statement, that masked tokens can only rise in rank relative to C3, is false when coverage is fractional: a masked token can be overtaken by a more-covered masked token. The judged invariants are the ones that hold for any coverage: equal group sizes, unmasked tokens keep their relative order and can only fall, no masked token falls behind an unmasked token it led, and the ROI's full-step count can only rise. The literal statement is judged for uniform coverage, where it holds.

C2.purpose: Dense Euler, 20 steps: naive 50 percent baseline

C3.purpose: Rank by need: need-only HSA baseline

C4.purpose: Rank by importance times need: primary Density test

C5.purpose: Rank by fractional coverage: importance without need

A1.purpose: C4 with hands and contact only

sphere_demo.inside_definition: latent elements of tokens with b = 1[m >= 0.1], via unpatchify
